newsitem.title: UK: MAM shares drop after low-end results.
newsitem.headline: MAM shares drop after low-end results.

text.p: Shares in Mercury Asset Management Plc dropped in early trading on Tuesday after the company posted first-half pre-tax profit at the low end of the range of analyst expectations.
The stock was down 25p at 11.17-1/2 stg by 0819 GMT, after on Friday closing at a record 11.44 stg.

"The figures are a bit disappointing but the stock has had a good run," said one analyst, who asked not to be named. "They are a strong outfit but the better growth in fund management is coming from Schroders."
MAM said pre-tax profit rose to 81.8 million stg from 63.6 million a year before, compared with expectations mostly in a range between 80 million stg and 85 million.
Funds under management rose to 85.9 billion stg from 70.9 billion, but margins were flat as operating costs rose due to factors including spending on systems and infrastructure.

The company said full-year results would, as usual, be influenced by the direction of markets, but it was "determined to maintain our long-term record of creating shareholder value through the profitable expansion of our business."
